summary: Careful preregistered paired evaluation of a GVR pipeline (gpt-5-mini + deterministic Batfish-style validator + ≤1 LLM repair) on intent→vendor-CLI tasks under shared_initial_candidate semantics. Planned N=300 pairs; 266 complete pairs analysed. Observed baseline pass-rate 260/266 (97.74%), guarded pass-rate 265/266 (99.62%), paired difference = 0.01880, exact McNemar two-sided p = 0.0625 (preregistered primary test, not significant at α=0.05). Paired bootstrap (B=10,000) CI = [0.00376, 0.03759] reported as supplementary. Repair invoked 6/300 tasks; median repair iterations = 0. Missingness/exclusions and provider-call accounting are archived; mandatory master-prompt locator and hashes are present in the Disclosure. The manuscript correctly states shared_initial_candidate semantics and limits inference to the executed estimand.
required_revisions: Insert the preregistration manifest SHA‑256 value (archived preregistration_sha256 = 46a223492f760950b3d06f475129ce21e52e296c4c2a1e09df3ccd50bec9f891) in every manuscript location that currently shows the placeholder 'preregistration manifest SHA‑256: )' (e.g., Abstract, Methodology, Disclosure) so the preregistration locator is explicit in the paper text. This change is resolvable from the supplied artifacts and must be made before finalisation.
optional_revisions: (Optional) As suggested previously, add a one‑paragraph supplementary table enumerating the six repair invocations (task id, validator failure code, short repair-change summary, final validity) drawn from the archived validator traces to illustrate typical repair yields (labelled descriptive).

(Optional) Report an ancillary robustness statistic (e.g., mid‑p or a one‑sided McNemar) explicitly labelled as post‑hoc/ancillary using the archived contingency counts, and/or provide a descriptive bootstrap interval for the derived NNT while clearly noting the high baseline-pass-rate caveats.
